Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verses 1–2:

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah; to Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾ (1)

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: Whatever is in the seven heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation prostrates to Him and magnifies Him.

* *

And His words: ﴿To Him belongs dominion﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, His authority is enforced, His decree is executed in them, and His command is carried out in them.

* *

And His words: ﴿And to Him belongs praise﴾

He says: And to Him belongs the praise of everything in them of creation, because all of the creatures in them do not recognize good except from Him, and they have no provider other than Him; so to Him belongs the praise of all of them. ﴿And He is over all things competent﴾ means: He is over every thing possessing power. He says: He creates what He wills, causes to die whom He wills, enriches whom He wills, impoverishes whom He wills, honors whom He wills, and humiliates whom He wills. Nothing He desires is impossible for Him, because He possesses complete power, by which nothing can overcome Him.

* *

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾ (2)

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: Allah ﴿who created you﴾, O people, and this is the one whose name is mentioned, ﴿among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ means: among you is one who disbelieves in his Creator and that He created him; ﴿and among you is a believer﴾ means: and among you is one who affirms Him and is certain that He is his Creator or Originator. ﴿And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾ means: Allah, who created you, is Seeing of your deeds, Knowing of them, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them. So fear Him, lest you oppose His command or His prohibition, and He seize you.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab narrated to us, he said: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, he said: Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to us, from Abu Tamim al-Jayshani, from Abu Dharr: "When the semen remains in the womb for forty nights, an angel of the souls comes, and he ascends with it to the Compeller in his palm, and says: 'My Lord, is this servant male or female?' Then God decrees to him what He decrees. Then he says: 'My Lord, is he wretched or happy?' So it is written what he will meet." He said: Abu Dharr recited the opening of Surat al-Taghabun, five verses.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and shaped you and perfected your shapes, and to Him is the final return﴾ (3)

He, the Exalted, says: He created the seven heavens and the earth with justice and equity. "And shaped you": that is, "and made you in a form, and made your form the best of forms." It has also been said that what is meant by this is His shaping of Adam and His creating him with His own hand.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth and shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾, that he said: "It means Adam, whom He created with His hand."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and to Him is the final return﴾:

He says: To Allah is the return of all of you, O people.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 4–6:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose. And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ (4)

His exalted remembrance says: Your Lord, O people, knows what is in the seven heavens and the earth, nothing of it being hidden from Him, ﴿and He knows what you conceal﴾ O people, among yourselves, of speech and deed, ﴿and what you disclose﴾ of that, by making it apparent. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾: He, great is His praise, has knowledge of the inner thoughts of His servants' hearts and what their souls harbour, which is more hidden than the secret, and nothing of that escapes Him. His exalted remembrance says to His servants: Beware lest you keep secret other than what you make known, or harbour in yourselves other than what you display, for your Lord is not hidden from anything of that, and He counts all of it and preserves all of it for you.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Has there not come to you the report of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment. (5) That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient. And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy. (6)﴾

His exalted remembrance says to the polytheists of Quraysh: Has there not come to you, O people, the report of those who disbelieved before you, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Abraham and the people of Lot? ﴿So they tasted the consequence of their affair﴾, so Allah's punishment befell them for their disbelief. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾: that is, for them is a painful, agonising punishment on the Day of Resurrection in the fire of Hell, in addition to what Allah made them taste in this world as the consequence of their disbelief.

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾

His exalted remembrance says: This which befell those who disbelieved before these polytheists, of the consequence of their disbelief, and the punishment their Lord prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection, is because their messengers, whom their Lord sent to them, used to come to them with clear proofs, evident signs and indications of the truth of what they called them to. They said to them, "Shall mere humans guide us?" out of arrogance, that messengers of God should be to them human beings like themselves, and out of arrogance toward following the truth, because a human like them was calling them to it. The report concerning "human" is stated in the plural, so it is said "yahdūnanā" (they guide us) and not "yahdīnā" (he guides us), because "basharun" (human), although in the singular form, carries the meaning of the plural.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away﴾

That is: they disbelieved in Allah and denied the messages of the messengers whom Allah sent to them, out of arrogance. ﴿And turned away﴾: that is, they turned their backs on the truth and did not accept it, and they averted themselves from what their messengers called them to. ﴿And Allah was self-sufficient﴾: that is, Allah was independent of them, of their faith in Him and His messengers, and He had no need of them for that. ﴿And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾: that is, Allah is independent of all His creation, praised by all of them for His beautiful favours upon them and His generous acts toward them.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah."﴾ (64:7)

He, may He be exalted, says: The disbelievers in Allah claim that Allah will never raise them up from their graves to Himself after their deaths. Ibn Umar used to say: "Zaʿama (claimed)" is the kunya (euphemistic epithet) of lying.

Muhammad ibn Nafi al-Basri narrated this to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Sufyan, from one of his companions, from Ibn Umar.

And His saying, ﴿Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected"﴾

He says to His Prophet ﷺ: Say to them, O Muhammad: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be raised from your graves." ﴿Then you will surely be informed of what you did﴾ means: then you will surely be told of your deeds which you performed in the world. ﴿And that is easy for Allah﴾ means: and raising you from your graves after your death is easy and simple for Allah.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (8)

He, the Exalted, says: So affirm belief in Allah and His Messenger, O polytheists who deny the Resurrection and His information to you that you will be resurrected after your death, and that after your decay you will be raised from your graves. "And the light which We have sent down" means: and believe in the light which We have sent down, namely this Qur'an which Allah sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ means: He, the Exalted, says, Allah is aware of your deeds, O people, encompassing them, counting all of them, nothing of them hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of them.

* *

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly. That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness – He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ (9)

He, the Exalted, says: And Allah is Acquainted with what you do. ﴿The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly﴾: the creation for the reckoning. ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ means: the assembly is a day of loss (ghabn) for the people of the Fire at the hands of the people of Paradise. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ – he said: it is the loss of the people of Paradise to the people of the Fire.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly﴾: it is the Day of Resurrection, and it is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain: the day when the people of Paradise lose out to the people of the Fire.

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ – it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which He magnified and warned His servants against.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness﴾

He, the Exalted, says: whoever affirms belief in Allah and acts in obedience to Him, and submits to His command and prohibition, ﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾ means: He will erase his sins from him. ﴿And admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ means: and He will admit him into orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow.

* *

And His saying: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾

He says: remaining therein forever, not dying, and not leaving them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is the great achievement﴾

He says: their abiding in the gardens we have described is the great salvation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 10:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever. And wretched is the destination.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Those who denied the oneness of Allah and denied His proofs, His evidences, and the verses of His Book which He sent down to His servant Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿They are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever﴾. He says: remaining in it eternally, neither dying therein nor coming out of it. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾. He says: And wretched is the thing to which one returns, which is Hellfire (Jahannam).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 11:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿No misfortune befalls except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: No one among creation is struck by a misfortune except by the permission of Allah, meaning: except by the decree of Allah and His determining of it upon him. ﴿And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾ means: whoever affirms Allah and knows that no one is struck by a misfortune except by the permission of Allah, Allah will guide his heart, meaning: Allah will grant success to his heart in submitting to His command and being content with His decree.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾: he means, He will guide his heart to certainty, so that he knows that what befell him would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have befallen him.

Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Washsha' al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Bashir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, who said: We were with Alqamah, and this verse was recited in his presence: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾, and he was asked about it, so he said: It is the man who is struck by a misfortune, and he knows that it is from Allah, so he submits to it and is content.

Isa ibn Uthman al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, who said: I was with Alqamah while he was reviewing the mushafs, and he passed by this verse: ﴿No misfortune befalls except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾, and he said: It is the man... then he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Alqamah, regarding His saying: ﴿No misfortune befalls except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾, he said: It is the man who is struck by a misfortune, and he knows that it is from Allah, so he submits to it and is content.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to me, from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Alqamah, the like of it; except that in his narration he said: he knows that it is from the decree of Allah, so he is content with it and submits.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾

It means: Allah is possessed of knowledge of all things, of what has occurred and what will occur, and of what is to occur before it occurs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 12–14:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification.﴾ ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And obey Allah﴾, O people, in His command and His prohibition, ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾ (ﷺ). ﴿But if you turn away﴾, meaning if you turn your backs on obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, being arrogant toward it, and do not obey Allah or His Messenger, ﴿then upon Our Messenger﴾ Muhammad ﴿is only the clear notification﴾, that it is a notification to you of what I sent him with. He, the Exalted, says: He has thus given you a warning by the notification, and Allah is the Protector of vengeance against whoever disobeys Him, opposes His command, and turns away from Him. ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him﴾. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: (O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you) … the verse. His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: Your wealth and your children, O people, are only a trial, meaning a tribulation upon you in this world.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

* *

As for His words: ﴿and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾

It means: Allah has with Him a great reward for you, if you oppose your children and your spouses in obedience to Allah your Lord, and obey Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, and render the right of Allah in your wealth. The great reward that is with Allah is Paradise.

* *

His words: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: Beware of Allah, O believers, and fear His punishment, and avoid His chastisement by performing His obligations and abstaining from His disobedience, and acting by what brings you near to Him, as much as you are able and as far as your capacity reaches.

It has been mentioned that His words: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ were revealed after His words: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾, as a lightening upon the Muslims, and that His words: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ abrogate (nasikh) His words: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey﴾, he said: This is a concession from Allah, and Allah is Merciful to His servants. Allah, may His praise be exalted, had previously revealed ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾, and the fear due to Him is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed. Then Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, lightened His burden upon His servants and revealed the concession after that, saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey﴾, in what you are able to do, O son of Adam. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged allegiance: to hear and obey in what you are able.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾, he said: it was abrogated by His words: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾.

Our explanation of the meaning of the abrogating and the abrogated (al-nasikh wa'l-mansukh) has already been given earlier, sufficient to dispense with repeating it in this place. However, in His words: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ there is no clear evidence that it abrogates His words: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾, since the latter may be understood as meaning: fear Allah with the fear due to Him as far as you are able; and there is no report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it abrogates it. Since this is so, it is obligatory to apply both together according to the various aspects of soundness that they admit.

* *

His words: ﴿and listen and obey﴾

It means: listen to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and obey him in what he commands you and forbids you. ﴿and spend, it is better for yourselves﴾ means: spend some of your wealth for your own selves, to rescue them from the punishment of Allah. The "good" (khayr) in this place means wealth.

* *

His words: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul – those are the successful﴾

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: Whoever Allah protects from the stinginess of his soul, and that is following its desires in what Allah has forbidden.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾, he said: the desire of his soul, by which he follows his desire and does not accept faith.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾, he said: that he intends to take the wealth of another and consume it. And His words: ﴿those are the successful﴾ mean: those who are protected from the stinginess of their souls are the prosperous, who attain their aims with their Lord.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 15–16:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾ (15) ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul – those are the successful﴾ (16).

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: Your wealth and your children, O people, are only a trial, meaning a tribulation upon you in this world.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, he said: it means a tribulation.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾

It means: Allah has with Him a great reward for you, if you oppose your children and your spouses in obedience to Allah your Lord, and obey Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, and render the right of Allah in your wealth. The great reward that is with Allah is Paradise.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾, and it is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 64, verses 17–18:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you, and Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing. (17) The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ (18)

His exalted mention says: "And if you spend in the way of Allah, spending well in it, and seek reward and recompense for your spending, your Lord will multiply that for you, giving you in place of one, seven hundred fold, or more than that, as much multiplication as He wills," ﴿and He will forgive you your sins﴾, that is, He will overlook your punishment for them, along with multiplying your spending which you spend in His way. ﴿And Allah is Most Appreciative﴾ means: Allah is possessed of appreciation toward those who spend in His way, by giving them a good recompense for what they spent in the world in His way. ﴿Forbearing﴾ means: forbearing toward those who disobey Him, by refraining from hastening to punish them. ﴿The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ means: He knows what the eyes of His servants do not see and what is hidden from their sight, and what they witness and see with their eyes. ﴿The Almighty﴾ means: severe in His retribution against those who disobey Him and oppose His command and prohibition. ﴿The All-Wise﴾ means: in His management of His creation and His turning of them to what benefits them.

End of the commentary on Surah At-Taghabun.
